newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Huge Norwich trade fuels stake sale talk.
newsitem.headline: Huge Norwich trade fuels stake sale talk.

text.p: Massive trade of over 75.8 million shares in Norwich Holdings Ltd on Thursday added fuel to earlier speculation that South African financial services group The Board of Executors Ltd was eyeing a stake in the life insurance company.
Dealers on the the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) said that banking group NBS Boland appeared to be the seller of the shares.
A spokeswoman for NBS said that the firm would make an announcement later on Thursday, but declined any further comment.
Norwich shares traded on the JSE on Thursday were worth around 661 million rand, dealers said. The stocks leapt 7.3 percent to 940 cents -- a new record high.
A dealer at Barnard Jacobs, the broking firm which sold a large quantity of the shares, said: "It was a corporate finance trade. Details of the deal will be in the newspapers tomorrow (Friday)."
Analysts earlier on Thursday downplayed speculation that BOE may have set its sights on taking a sizable stake in Norwich to secure a foothold in the insurance industry.

Newspaper reports on Thursday quoted unnamed sources saying a complex transaction may be in the offing, whereby BOE may buy a stake in the insurer from the NBS Boland Bank group, which holds a 25 percent interest.
Terry Norton, the managing director of NBS Holdings, declined to comment.
Boland and BOE could not be reached for comment.

"I don't see why they would want to buy into Norwich...The (insurance) industry is in a material phase where you are not seeing real growth on the recurring premium side, although the single premium side is showing a bit of growth," said Dave Southey, an analyst at stockbroker Edey Rogers.
The paper said BOE, a financial services firm which offers asset management and investment services to private and corporate clients, has long wanted to add an insurance arm to its portfolio.
It said BOE was understood to have been a contender for Protea Assurance's life business which was last year bought by Commercial Union of South Africa Ltd CUAJ.J for 250 million rand.

Norwich on Monday issued a cautionary notice to say it was in talks. The paper said NBS Holdings and Boland Bank Ltd, which merged in December to create South Africa's fifth largest bank, were still covered by cautionaries.
